DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC).

The clinical picture of a 32-year-old female (note: the untrusted text says "male", but PBC is overwhelmingly common in middle-aged women; if the patient is indeed male, this could be a rare variant or misidentified disease) with chronic cholestasis (elevated Alkaline Phosphatase), severe pruritus, and a history of autoimmune conditions (ulcerative colitis) strongly suggests an autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts. The elevated Alkaline Phosphatase with only mild elevation in transaminases and normal bilirubin is classic for early-stage PBC.
